title: Your people
hook: An app can't hug you on Eid. Today you map the people who can.

screens.text: Three days to Day 90. This app has been with you every day, but it can't sit next to you at iftar or hug you on Eid. People can. Today you map who yours are, and who you'll call.

screens.prompt: A large study of American converts asked what helps faith grow [Yaqeen 2025]. Which were the strongest supports? Tap all that apply.

options.feedback: Yes. Friends who share your faith were one of the strongest supports.
Yes. Belonging to a masjid helps faith grow.
Yes. A good imam was one of the three strongest supports.

options.text: Studying alone as much as possible
options.feedback: Not quite. Learning helps, but people made the biggest difference: friends, a masjid and a good imam.

screens.text: **People keep faith alive.** The Prophet ﷺ described believers as bricks in one wall, each holding the others up [Bukhari 481]. You were never meant to do this alone.

screens.title: Your community map has four rings. Tap each one.

cards.back: {{mentor.name}} or the imam, for questions and hard days.
One or two Muslims you can text, eat with, pray next to.
The masjid, a weekly class or study circle (*halaqa*), a volunteer spot.
They still count. Keep them close and be kind [Q 31:15].

screens.prompt: Match each moment to who you'd turn to.

pairs.right: Your masjid, or a family who invited you

screens.prompt: Draw your community map. Write the names (or places) in each ring: guide, friends, places, family. Compare it with the circle you drew on Day 18. Which ring has grown? Which one is thin, and who could fill it?

screens.text: **Plan for the hard days now.** About four in ten converts feel lonely during Ramadan or Eid [Yaqeen 2025]. Don't wait to be invited: ask someone this month, "Where are you for Eid? Can I come?"
bubbles: A real friend makes your faith easier, not your life smaller.

screens.prompt: Real community, or a red flag to tell {{mentor.name}} about?

items.text: A sister or brother from class invites you to iftar with their family
items.why: That's community: someone making your faith easier and your circle bigger.

items.text: Someone says you should stop seeing your family now that you're Muslim
items.why: Pushing you toward isolation isn't community. Tell {{mentor.name}}.

items.text: Someone you just met keeps urging you to get married quickly
items.why: Pressure toward a quick marriage isn't community. Tell {{mentor.name}}.

items.text: A friend saves you a seat at the weekly class
items.why: That's what real friends do: they make showing up easier.

items.text: Someone at the masjid keeps asking you for money
items.why: Pressure about money isn't community. Tell {{mentor.name}}.

screens.situation: Luis has gone to the masjid for weeks, but he leaves right after the prayer and still doesn't know anyone. What's his best next step?

options.text: Join the weekly class or a volunteer shift, and stay ten minutes after one prayer to say salam
options.feedback: Yes. Classes and volunteering put him next to the same faces every week. That's how friendships start.

options.text: Keep coming and wait for someone to approach him
options.feedback: Not quite. Some people will, but many are shy too. One small step from him speeds it up.

options.text: Give up on the masjid and stick to online groups
options.feedback: Online can help, but it can't replace faces you see each week. Friends at the masjid are a big protector.

screens.text: **Choose your company with care.** The Prophet ﷺ said a person tends to follow the ways of their close friend, so look carefully at who that is [Abu Dawud 4833].
bubbles: That doesn't mean dropping old friends. It means making sure some of your closest people help you pray, not skip it.
{teen}**Under 18?** Meet people at masjid events and classes, in public spaces, and keep {{mentor.name}} in the loop.{/teen}

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Religious Muslim friends, attachment to a masjid and a capable imam were the strongest predictors of converts' faith growing; about 40% felt lonely in Ramadan or Eid; 78% made friends at the masjid [Yaqeen 2025, via Research Notes - Retention R1].
- Believers support each other like bricks in a wall [Bukhari 481].
- Keep kind ties with family, even when they don't share your faith [Q 31:15].
- A person tends to follow their close friend's way, so choose closest friends carefully [Abu Dawud 4833]. This doesn't mean cutting off non-Muslim friends.
- The community map: guide (mentor/imam), friends, places (masjid, class, volunteering), family and old friends.

**Likely questions**
- *"How do I make Muslim friends as an adult?"* Same faces every week: one class, one volunteer shift, staying after one prayer. Suggest one concrete step and offer to draft a message.
- *"I feel like an outsider at my masjid."* Validate it; it's common, especially at masjids organized around one culture. Suggest the mentor, a convert circle if the masjid has one, or another nearby masjid's class. Route harsh treatment to the mentor.
- *"I have nowhere to go for Eid."* Encourage asking the mentor or a friend now; many families welcome guests. The masjid's Eid prayer is open to all. Don't invent events.
- *"My old friends don't get it."* Keep the good ones; be kind; step back only from what pulls you away from your faith.

**Escalate:** anyone pressuring the convert into marriage, money or cutting off family (route to the mentor, Spec §6.2 rule 12); being thrown out or unsafe at home (safety rule first).

**Don't**
- Don't tell anyone to cut off family or non-Muslim friends.
- Don't promise specific events, classes or families at the masjid.
- For under-18s: suggest only public masjid settings and mentor-included contact, per safeguarding.
sourcesMd:
- [Bukhari 481](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:481): believers are like a building whose parts hold each other up.
- Qur'an [31:15](https://quran.com/31/15): keep company with your parents in this world with kindness.
- [Abu Dawud 4833](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:4833) (hasan, al-Albani): a person follows the way of their close friend.
- Yaqeen Institute, *Becoming Muslim: The Lives of American Converts to Islam* (2025), via Research Notes - Retention and Convert Voices R1: protective factors; loneliness in Ramadan and Eid.
- Research Notes - Retention and Convert Voices: isolation after the shahada; friends and masjid attachment as protective factors.
- The New Muslims Field Guide ch. 11 (the masjid), ch. 12 (the company you keep).
